title: Coverage counts raw records outside the selected product
description: `raw_counts` scans `tick_trade` by session time without restricting rows to the requested product’s shape. `_session_row` then treats every returned instrument as part of the comparison, so records belonging to another product can appear as raw-only mismatches and make `coverage --product …` exit 3. Scope the raw scan to the selected shape and add a test with unrelated-product records in the same sessions.

title: Coverage compares different database snapshots
description: Ledger totals and raw counts execute separately on the autocommit connection provided by `store_context.py`. If an ingest commits between these reads, coverage compares the old ledger with new raw rows and falsely reports corruption, exiting 3. Run the comparison in a read-only, repeatable-read transaction and add a concurrent-ingest regression test.

title: An unknown availability edge can report caught up
description: When a tier and start are configured but neither an explicit end nor an observed edge exists, `wanted` becomes `None`. With no held units, the verdict list is empty, yet `caught_up([], wanted=True)` returns `True`. Report an unknown/not-caught-up result rather than claiming completeness without an established range.

title: Coverage repeatedly scans all instrument-session keys on the event loop
description:
Each session reconstructs and scans every ledger and raw key, making report construction quadratic in the session count. This synchronous work runs inside `build_coverage`; an isolated benchmark of the actual function took approximately 0.87 seconds for 500 sessions × 100 instruments. Group counts by session once and offload substantial CPU work; add a coverage-specific load test.

Tests could not run: the available environment lacks `psycopg`, and pytest capture requires temporary-file access unavailable in this read-only sandbox.

title: Scope raw counts to the requested product
description: `raw_counts` counts every `tick_trade` row in the requested time window, while `ledger_totals` is filtered to the selected product’s request shape. Once the tick database contains more than one product, coverage for each product will include other products’ rows as raw-only mismatches. This will affect the default all-products command as well as `--product`; restrict the raw scan to the selected shape’s instruments.

title: Missing calendar configuration is reported as a storage outage
description: The read path passes `calendar_url(settings)` into the calendar read. When the production DB URL is unset, `calendar_url` raises `TickCalendarError`, which `exit_code_for` maps to storage exit 4. The status/coverage contract and `READ_EPILOG` classify configuration problems as preflight exit 1, reserving 4 for an unreachable database. Map the missing setting to preflight rather than outage.

title: Calendar pool timeouts escape the storage error mapping
description: `calendar_sessions` translates `psycopg.OperationalError`, but not `psycopg_pool.PoolTimeout`. If the production calendar connection pool cannot provide a connection before its timeout, that exception is not mapped by `exit_code_for` and escapes as a traceback instead of the documented storage exit 4. Handle the pool timeout as a calendar storage failure.

title: Add a load test for the coverage read path
description: Coverage performs a raw `tick_trade` count over a user-selected date range, but the added tests exercise correctness only; the load test in the project covers ingest, not this read path. Because this database/network path can scan a large hypertable, add a realistic load test with an explicit latency or resource bound.

title: The coverage "proof" compares the ledger and the raw rows over different populations
description:
`ledger_totals()` is restricted to the shape's *current* units (`_SHAPE_WHERE`: dataset, symbols, stype_in, stored tiers, `COVERAGE_PREDICATE`), while `raw_counts()` counts **every** row in `tick_trade` whose `ts_event` falls in the session window, with no `unit_id`, shape or product restriction. The comparison in `tick_coverage._session_row` then pairs the two per instrument.

The module docstring's premise — "Raw rows change after commit only through supersession (whose ledger is excluded) or by hand, so a mismatch is evidence of an out-of-band edit or a defect" — does not hold: `adopt` accepts any batch job, and a unit ingested for a *different* shape of the same product (e.g. `symbols = [ESZ4]`, `stype_in = raw_symbol`) writes rows with the same `instrument_id` into `tick_trade`. Those rows are counted as "raw" for the universe's shape but are absent from its ledger, so `mt data tick coverage` would report a mismatch and exit 3 for a database that is in fact consistent. The same asymmetry can mask a real defect if a shape's rows were deleted while another shape's rows keep the count non-zero.

The fix is to scope `raw_counts` to the same units the ledger is scoped to (join through `tick_archive_unit`/`tick_request` with `_SHAPE_WHERE` and `COVERAGE_PREDICATE`, or pass the current unit ids in), so both sides of the proof describe one population.

title: `status`/`coverage` exit 4 when the held days reach the calendar's populated horizon
description:
`_scope` builds its calendar bounds from the held unit days as `utc_midnight(d)` and `utc_midnight(d + 1 day)`, then calls `calendar_sessions(...)` → `TradingCalendar.sessions_between`, which refuses with `OutOfPopulatedRangeError` unless *both* bounds lie inside `[first_open, last_close]` (`trading_calendar.py::_require_populated`).

Two consequences:

* the lower bound `midnight(earliest held day)` is earlier than the calendar's `first_open` when the earliest held unit is the calendar's first session date (that session opens at 22:00, so `midnight` of the same day precedes it);
* the upper bound `midnight(latest held day + 1)` is later than `last_close` whenever the latest held unit is the calendar's last session date — the normal case for an ingest that has caught up to the horizon.

Either case raises `TickCalendarError`, which `exit_code_for` maps to exit 4, so the whole command fails with "calendar … outside populated sessions" instead of reporting the status. This is the same bound rule 225 TD7 established for ingest (`test/unit/data/tick/test_session_days.py`: "ingest's `sessions_between(d, d+1)` never passes the horizon"), where the offending day is instead reported as a per-unit `session_boundary` check failure (`ingest_plan.Calendars.frame`). `build_coverage` widens the same exposure by querying from `utc_midnight(start - timedelta(days=1))`.

Clamping the bounds to the populated span (or intersecting them with the sessions actually held) would keep the verb usable at the edges.

title: The `degraded` count is attached to the wrong bucket line
description:
The bucket rows are appended in a loop over `_BUCKET_ROWS`, and then

```python
lines[-1] += f"   (degraded {p.degraded})"
```

appends the degraded **condition** count to the last bucket line — which is the `edge unknown` row. The output therefore reads `edge unknown 2   (degraded 1)`, which a reader will take as a qualifier of the edge-unknown bucket rather than as the count of degraded days. `degraded` counts sessions whose worst condition is `degraded` (see `tick_status_build._product_status`), which is unrelated to any bucket. It deserves its own line, e.g. `degraded sessions: N`.

title: No load test covers the new bounded `tick_trade` scan
description: The slice adds a read path over the `tick_trade` hypertable (`raw_counts`: a `count(*)` over the range's first open to last close joined against the session array). The project rules require a load test for code on the database/environment paths that asserts on latency, throughput or resource bounds, and the slice already has a load tier (`test/load/test_225_tick_ingest_nfr.py` covers ingest). Nothing exercises `coverage` at scale: a wide `--start/--end` range, a session array with hundreds of entries, or the resulting scan cost on a multi-chunk hypertable is untested. The range is unbounded by the CLI (only `end > start` is checked), so an operator can ask for a decade-wide scan with no statement timeout on the connection.
